readout_other: Electrode-free video and EMG motor-evoked potentials (M1 parameter finding); c-Fos immunolabelling; [18F]-FDG microPET imaging; LC-HRMS brain metabolomics; nest-building, reward-maze and open-field behavioural tests
direction_notes: USNS of M1 produced dose-dependent motor-evoked responses; acute/chronic USNS of the infralimbic cortex increased local and distant (striatum, thalamus, hippocampus, PAG, raphe) c-Fos expression and FDG metabolism, reduced anxiety-related behaviours (open-field mobility/center-crossings, nest-building) but did not improve anhedonia (reward-maze) relative to fluoxetine.

exposures.label: single-pulse USNS of primary motor cortex M1 for parameter optimization

timing.protocol_description: Single-pulse USNS (160-ms tone bursts) was delivered over left M1 at peak negative pressures stepped from 50 to 500 kPa in 50-kPa increments. In a first subset (n=20), 10 pulses 10 s apart were delivered per pressure step via a threshold-hunting algorithm (electrode-free motor response scoring). In a second subset (n=10, EMG), pressures from 350-500 kPa were tested; 400 kPa (160-msec pulse) gave the best combination of motor success, MEP amplitude, reliability and focality and was adopted for subsequent infralimbic-cortex USNS.

exposures.label: acute and chronic repeated USNS of the infralimbic cortex (IL)

target.label: infralimbic cortex (IL), the sgACC equivalent in rodents

timing.protocol_description: Acute USNS was a 10-min session of 60 pulses (each pulse 400 kPa, 160-msec) repeated at a rate of 0.1 Hz over the infralimbic cortex under 1% isoflurane. For chronic USNS, one such session was applied every day for 5 consecutive days (day 29-33), totalling 300 stimuli over 60 min; a Sham group received the same procedure with the transducer deactivated.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Thirty mice were used for setting-up optimal US neurostimulation (USNS) parameters with motor response measurements, determined with: 1) electrode-free video recordings of the targeted limb (n=20) and 2) electromyography (n=10).
source_quotes.exposures[0].fundamental_frequency_khz: US waves were generated using a single-element transducer with a central frequency of 500 kHz, coupled to a water-filled collimated column (d=10 mm) and operated on a stereotaxic frame.
source_quotes.exposures[0].free_field.pressure_kpa: In a cohort of thirty mice positioned in the stereotaxic frame under gaseous anesthesia (0.1- 1% isoflurane), peak negative pressures ranging from 50 to 500 kPa by steps of 50 kPa were delivered from the transducer (25) (Figure 1A).
source_quotes.exposures[0].timing.sonication_duration_: The transducer had a diameter of 38 mm and was focused at 65 mm, driven with an electrical signal generated by an arbitrary waveform generator set for 160-millisecond pulses and amplified with a power amplifier.
source_quotes.exposures[1].fundamental_frequency_khz: Ultrasound stimuli were generated using a single-element transducer focused at 65 mm (active diameter of 38 mm, Imasonic, Besançon, France) with a central frequency of 500 kHz and a fractional bandwidth of 58%.
source_quotes.exposures[1].free_field.pressure_kpa: From single-pulse USNS data and previous studies (16), the pattern of acute USNS was constructed as a 10-min session of 60 USNS pulses (1 pulse: 400 kPa, 160-msec) repeated at a rate of 0.1 Hz and delivered over the prefrontal cortex under 1% isoflurane anesthesia.

source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: This constituted one treatment session of chronic USNS (or “acute USNS”); one session was applied every day for 5 consecutive days from day 29 to day 33 to constitute the chronic protocol of chronic USNS (total of 300 US stimuli over 60 min).

flags.reason: Paper gives group sizes for separate sub-experiments (M1 parameter-finding: 20 electrode-free + 10 EMG; acute USNS: 4; chronic USNS: 15) rather than one exposed total; listed rather than summed.
Varies by sub-experiment: single session for M1 parameter-finding and acute USNS, 5 daily sessions for chronic USNS.
Paper states a skull attenuation coefficient (6.32±2.18% at 500 kHz) used to derate pressure inside the brain but does not give the resulting derated kPa value for specific stimulation levels.
Paper equates the infralimbic cortex (IL) with the rodent sgACC counterpart; target term chosen on that explicit equivalence rather than the vmPFC/prelimbic hierarchy.
